# `property-became-required`

Property became required

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-became-required` (both directions), `property-became-required-in-request`, `property-became-required-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An optional property is now required.

## Why this default

In requests: clients that didn't send it are rejected. In responses: clients now always receive it, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`property-became-required`](../../test/cases/property-became-required/): An optional request property became required.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
+       required:
+       - name
```

Findings:

- `property-became-required-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  property-became-required: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, keep it optional with a default.
